sentences.text:
Shri Akshansh Mehra, learned counsel for respondent No.
 Order

The appellant has filed this Misc. Appeals under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 18.12.2018 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Dewas (M.P.) in Claim Case No.146/2017 challenging the inadequacy of compensation.
2. The brief facts of the case are that on 31.08.2016, the appellant was riding his motorcycle from Dewas to his home Siroliya.

At around 5:45 PM, when he reached the Gram Panchayat square on Rajoda - Kelod Road, Rajoda, respondent No.1, driving his motorcycle bearing registration number MP-41-MR-2248 came in a rash and negligent manner from wrong direction and hit the motorcycle of the appellant.
As a result of the accident, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
He was initially taken to M.G. Hospital, Dewas and then transferred to Sanskar Hospital, Dewas, where he remained admitted from 31.08.2016 to 07.09.2016.

Thereafter, the police registered an FIR for the accident under Sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC with the FIR being marked as (Ex.P-2).
3.
The appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the above mentioned accident.

After considering the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:16884 2 MA-1506-2019 evidence available on record, the Claims Tribunal assessed the total compensation at Rs.2,05,800/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the assessment of permanent disability in paras 21 to 26 of the award is not correct and proper.

He further submits that while the overall permanent disability has been taken at 10% by the Claims Tribunal, paras 21 and 23 of the award clearly indicate that the appellant has suffered 49.5% disability in his right leg.

sentences.text: He submits that the appellant was engaged in agricultural work and was also running a business of selling of milk, which he duly proved.
The appellant deposed as AW-1 before the Claims Tribunal and claimed that he was earning Rs.2,00,000/- per month from agriculture and Rs.10,000/- per month from his milk business.
However, as the appellant did not produce any documents establishing his income, the Claims Tribunal treated him as an unskilled labourer.

The Claims Tribunal recorded the finding that on the date of accident, the appellant was 45 years old and classified him as a labourer, assessing his monthly income at Rs.6,000/- per month on a notional basis.

6. The counsel submits hat even if the appellant is considered as a labourer, the overall loss of earning capacity assessed at 10% is not sustainable in the given clinching evidence that has come on record and which was duly discussed by the Claims Tribunal in para 23 of the award.
This evidence establishes that the appellant sustained 49.5% disability in his right leg.
7. He further submits that the assessment of income at Rs.6,000/- per month treating the appellant as an unskilled labourer is also on the lower side.

His submission is that even for an unskilled labourer at the relevant time (i.e. on the date of accident 31.08.2016), the minimum wages prescribed by the State Legal Services Authority for unskilled laboueres was Rs.6,850/- per month.
Thus, he submits that the assessment of income is on the lower side.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:16884 3 MA-1506-2019 8.
The counsel further submits that in view of Exs.P-22 and the statement of Dr. Jayant Sharma (AW-2), it is clearly established that the appellant remained under treatment for about one month.
Therefore, the loss of income during the treatment period should have been awarded.
However, the Claims Tribunal has not awarded anything for the same.

9. He also submits that the medical bills for the appellant's treatment were not accepted by the Claims Tribunal solely because the appellant did not produce prescriptions for those bills, which is not sustainable for the reason that the given that the bills were not disputed by any of the respondents.
10. Lastly, the counsel submits that nothing has been added for future prospects in the income of appellant.
Additionally, the Claims Tribunal has not awarded any compensation for pain and suffering even though the finding of disability and grievous injury was made by the Claims Tribunal itself.
As such, he requests for an enhancement of the compensation accordingly.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 / Insurance Company supports the findings of the award and states that the Claims Tribunal correctly assessed the appellant's overall disability at 10%, considering that the 49.5% permanent disability is only in relation to his right leg.

Therefore,
keeping in mind that the body has four limbs, the disability should be taken as 10% overall.
12. He further submits that the treatment bills cannot be accepted in the absence of prescriptions for the same, and thus, the Claims Tribunal correctly rejected those bills.

Additionally, as the appellant Mukut Chaudhary vs Rakesh Rathod on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105863752/
2 has already been compensated for permanent disability, there was no need for further compensation under the head of loss of income.

sentences.text: Consequently, he submits that no interference is warranted in the award.

13. Heard learned counsel for respective parties and perused the record.
14.

It is evident from the discussion in paras 21 to 23 of the award that the Claims Tribunal has not disbelieved that the appellant' has sustained 49.5% permanent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:16884 4 MA-1506-2019 disability.

The Tribunal after referring to the statement of Dr. Jayant Sharma (AW-2) and considering the permanent disability certificate (Ex. P-86)
concluded that the appellant suffered 49.5% permanent disability in his right leg.
However, when assessing the overall disability, the Tribunal has taken it at 10%.
15. The Claims Tribunal has also considered the appellant to be a labourer and as per para 31 of the award, the appellant himself claims to be an agriculturist.
It is important to assess whether the 49.5% permanent disability would impact his ability to perform his job, especially if he is treated as an unskilled labourer.
16. In the considered view of this Court, a labourer with 49.5% permanent disability in his right leg would not be able to perform his duties effectively.
Therefore, treating the appellant's loss of earning capacity at 10% is not commensurate with the extent of injuries suffered by the appellant.

Hence,
the permanent disability with respect to the loss of earning capacity is assessed at 20%.

17. As regards the submission of the counsel for the appellant for future prospects, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, future prospects have been added.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the appellant was 45 years of age on the date of accident, 25% is to be added in the income of the appellant.

18. Thus, after above modifications, the compensation for permanent disability resulting in loss of income would come to Rs.2,87,700/-.
19.

As regards the medical expenses, in the considered view of this Court, since Exs. P-50 and P-70 were neither disputed nor alleged to be fabricated, there was no reason for the Tribunal to discard them.
These were accepted as evidence to demonstrate the expenses incurred for the operations of the appellant.
Additionally, the medical bills for treatment, Exs. P-33 to P-37 and Exs.P-49 to P-75 and P-78, have not been alleged to be fabricated.
Therefore, there was no reasons for the Tribunal to discard these documents.

As such, the expenses incurred for the operations and medical NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:16884 5 MA-1506-2019 bills are also hereby awarded, which total Rs.22,500/- and Rs.9,184/- respectively.
20. As regards the loss of income, the counsel for the appellant appears to be correct.
The appellant underwent repeated surgeries and sustained 49.5% permanent disability.

He must have remained under treatment for an extended period and consequently suffered a loss of income during this Mukut Chaudhary vs Rakesh Rathod on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105863752/
3 period.

entities.text: Mukut Chaudhary vs Rakesh Rathod on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, an amount of Rs.75,000/- is hereby awarded for the same.

21. Apart from this, for pain and suffering, an amount of Rs,15,000/- is awarded and for special diet,
attendant and conveyance, an amount of Rs.30,000/- (Rs.10,000/- for each) is hereby awarded.
22. Thus, after the above modifications and additions, the total compensation amounts to Rs.5,29,384/-.
The Claims Tribunal had awarded Rs.2,05,800/-, meaning the enhance amount of Rs.3,23,584/- is to be paid to the appellant over and above what has already been paid by the Claims Tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal.
23. With above terms, the appeal stands partly allowed.
24. It is noted that the appellant has valued the claim at Rs.3,00,000/-.
Therefore, the appellant is directed to pay the deficit court fees within 15 days from today.
